title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. Grothendieck is studying automorphisms u of the profinite free group \hat\Pi_{0,3} = \hat\pi_1(P^1 - {0,1,\infty}). The loops l_0, l_1, l_\infty satisfy l_0 l_\infty l_1 = 1. He asks that u be compatible, up to inner automorphisms, with the S_3 symmetry. That symmetry is generated by the order-3 rotation \rho (l_0 -> l_\infty -> l_1, with \rho(\epsilon_0) = ...) and the involution \sigma_\infty (with \sigma_\infty(l_0) = l_1). He also asks that u act on the inertia generators by raising them to a power p \in \hat Z^* (the cyclotomic character). These are the 'equations des lacets'.

First step (previous page). Compatibility with \rho leads to a non-abelian 1-cocycle equation \zeta\rho(\zeta)\rho^2(\zeta) = 1 for Z/3 acting on \hat F_2. Grothendieck assumes, to be checked later, that there are exactly two cohomology classes. The first is the trivial one, \zeta = \lambda\rho(\lambda)^{-1} (55). The second is \zeta = \lambda l_0^{-1}\rho(\lambda)^{-1} (56).

This page, case A (\zeta of the form (55)).
- Compatibility with \sigma_\infty reduces to finding g_0 with \sigma_\infty(g_0)^{-1} g_0 = h_0 (58), where h_0 = \rho(\lambda)\lambda^{-1} l_0^\gamma = \xi^{-1} l_0^\gamma, \xi = \lambda\rho(\lambda)^{-1} and \gamma = (p-1)/2.
- This is a Z/2 non-abelian H^1 problem. g_0 is unique iff the fixed subgroup \hat\Pi_{0,3}^{\sigma_\infty} is trivial. The margin queries exactly this.
- He claims g_0 exists iff the cocycle condition \sigma_\infty(h_0) h_0 = 1 holds (59).
- Substituting h_0 = \xi^{-1} l_0^\gamma and \sigma_\infty(l_0) = l_1 gives \sigma_\infty(\xi)^{-1} l_1^\gamma \xi^{-1} l_0^\gamma = 1. That is, \sigma_\infty(\xi) = l_1^\gamma \xi^{-1} l_0^\gamma (60).

Corollary. Automorphisms u, taken up to \hat\Pi_{0,3}-conjugation of the \rho-data, correspond bijectively to pairs (\lambda, p) \in L_0\\hat\Pi_{0,3} x \hat Z^* satisfying (60) with \xi = \lambda\rho(\lambda)^{-1} and \gamma = (p-1)/2. Here L_0 is the closed subgroup generated by l_0. Further:
- For fixed \lambda there is at most one \gamma, so p is determined by \lambda.
- One needs the extra condition that 2\gamma+1 is a unit, i.e. there exists \gamma' with 2\gamma\gamma' + \gamma + \gamma' = 0. This is equivalent to (2\gamma+1)(2\gamma'+1) = 1, since \hat Z is 2-torsion-free.
- The next page checks independence of the choice of \lambda in its L_0-coset. It then summarises the procedure: solve (A) \xi\rho(\xi)\rho^2(\xi) = 1, then (C) \sigma_\infty(\xi) = l_1^\gamma \xi^{-1} l_0^\gamma.

Modern reading. This is a parametrisation of the Grothendieck–Teichmuller-type group by a pair (p, \xi). It has a pure 3-cycle relation \xi\rho(\xi)\rho^2(\xi) = 1, while the exponent m = (p-1)/2 sits in a twisted 2-cycle relation. By contrast, Drinfeld's GT has the plain 2-cycle f(x,y)f(y,x) = 1 and the hexagon f(z,x) z^m f(y,z) y^m f(x,y) x^m = 1 with m = (\lambda-1)/2. Both are ways of encoding S_3-equivariance of the automorphism, and the exponent (\lambda-1)/2 appears in the same role.
errors: The existence claim 'g_0 exists iff \sigma_\infty(h_0)h_0 = 1' needs triviality of the non-abelian H^1(Z/2, \hat F_2) for the swap involution. The page does not justify this. It is true: \hat F_2 \rtimes Z/2 is the profinite free product \hat Z * Z/2, and finite subgroups of free profinite products are conjugate into factors (Herfort–Ribes), so every involution of the form h s is F-conjugate to s.

Uniqueness of g_0 requires the fixed subgroup of \sigma_\infty to be trivial. Grothendieck flags this himself with the marginal '?'. It is true, since the centraliser of s in \hat Z * Z/2 is <s>, but it is unproved here.
The two-class claim for the Z/3 cocycle equation (previous page) is explicitly an assumption. It is correct, since \hat F_2 \rtimes Z/3 is the profinite completion of Z/3 * Z/3.

ideas.what: Reduction of the compatibility of u with the involution \sigma_\infty to a non-abelian Z/2-coboundary equation \sigma_\infty(g_0)^{-1} g_0 = h_0, with existence governed by the cocycle condition \sigma_\infty(h_0) h_0 = 1
ideas.modern_name: non-abelian group cohomology H^1(Z/2, \hat F_2) / conjugacy of torsion in profinite free products
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Serre, Cohomologie galoisienne); torsion in profinite free products: Herfort–Ribes

ideas.what: Parametrisation of S_3-compatible automorphisms of \hat F_2 by pairs (p, \xi): a pure 3-cycle \xi\rho(\xi)\rho^2(\xi) = 1, plus the twisted 2-cycle relation \sigma_\infty(\xi) = l_1^\gamma \xi^{-1} l_0^\gamma with \gamma = (p-1)/2, p \in \hat Z^*
ideas.modern_name: defining relations of the Grothendieck–Teichmuller group \hat{GT} (2-cycle and hexagon relations with m = (\lambda-1)/2)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only announces the program of describing Gal(\bar Q/Q) via its action on the tower of \hat\pi_1 of moduli spaces (genus 0, n = 4,5); the explicit relations are not there.

ideas.what: Uniqueness of \gamma given \xi, so the cyclotomic exponent p is determined by the group-theoretic part \lambda; unit condition 2\gamma+1 \in \hat Z^* rewritten as 2\gamma\gamma' + \gamma + \gamma' = 0
ideas.modern_name: injectivity of (\lambda, f) -> f on GT / the character \lambda being determined by f

missed.claim: In unpublished notes continuing La Longue Marche (c. 1981, roughly a decade before Drinfeld's 1990 paper), Grothendieck derives by hand an explicit system of equations for automorphisms of \hat\Pi_{0,3} compatible with the S_3 symmetry. It features the exponent \gamma = (p-1)/2 with p cyclotomic. This is essentially Drinfeld's m = (\lambda-1)/2, and it is placed in a variant 2-cycle relation rather than the hexagon. This is a concrete pre-Drinfeld appearance of a GT-type presentation.
missed.quote: \sigma_\infty(\xi)=l_1^\gamma.\xi^{-1}.l_0^\gamma ... \gamma=\frac{p-1}{2} ... il existe au plus une \gamma\in\hat{\mathbb Z} tel que la relation (60) soit valable
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit: it documents how far Grothendieck got toward \hat{GT} before Drinfeld/Ihara. The variant parametrisation (pure 3-cycle for \xi, exponent moved into the involution relation) could be compared with Drinfeld's to check the equivalence of the two presentations.

missed.claim: Case B (the non-trivial Z/3 cohomology class \zeta = \lambda l_0^{-1}\rho(\lambda)^{-1}) and the margin question about \sigma_\infty-fixed points are left open on this page.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: These are minor and settled by Herfort–Ribes-type results on profinite free products. Case B might correspond to a twisted (non-tautological) family worth comparing with known GT normalisations.

deep.surprise_reason: The page derives an explicit GT-like system, including the characteristic exponent (p-1)/2, in unpublished notes that likely predate Drinfeld. The individual steps are routine non-abelian cohomology. The historical anticipation is notable but may already be partly known to specialists (Schneps, Lochak) who have studied the Longue Marche material.
transcription_corrections: (60) should read \sigma_\infty(\xi) = l_1^\gamma \xi^{-1} l_0^\gamma: the preceding line gives \sigma_\infty(\xi)^{-1} l_1^\gamma \xi^{-1} l_0^\gamma = 1, and the next page's (C) has \xi^{-1}.
The label struck before \sigma_\infty(\xi)^{-1}... appears to be '(58)' overwritten, not a new equation number.

'Corollaire: Les u qui me[?] changent[?] par la conjugaison' is better read as 'Les u qui ne changent pas ... à \hat\Pi_{0,3}-conjugaison près de \rho', i.e. u normalising the \rho-data up to inner conjugation.
'L_0\backslash\hat\Pi_{0,3}': L_0 is the closed subgroup generated by l_0, acting on the left, as confirmed by the next page's NB (\lambda -> l_0^\alpha\lambda).
